readme.purpose: Reviewed overrides for one known site where the imagery or the data sources are known to mislead the tool (for example a road that OSM draws wrongly). The file ships empty: the tool adds no real entries. Every entry is a deliberate human decision.

schema.entry_id: unique text id of the entry
schema.scope: exactly one of site_id | zone_id | osm_way_id (an integer) naming where the entry applies
schema.field: the fact it applies to (a call 1 field or a measured width); never a mandatory start field (road_type, posted_speed_mph, traffic_volume, lane_closure)
schema.action: SET_VALUE (needs value) or FORCE_UNKNOWN (takes no value)
schema.value: the override value, SET_VALUE only, one scalar
schema.proposed_by_role: SME or ADMIN, chosen from a dropdown

rules: An entry applies only to its named site, zone or OSM way and only to its named field.
Every use is listed in the run trace (entry id, scope, field, action, original outcome and value).
The sha256 of this file is recorded in the run trace.
A malformed file or entry fails closed: nothing is applied and the run stops with SITE_EXCEPTIONS_MALFORMED.
Two entries for the same field at the same site fail closed.

Roles are SME, APPROVER and ADMIN, chosen from a dropdown and recorded as: role selected, not verified. The SME proposes and the ADMIN enters; the admin can do everything for now; the APPROVER is for rule pack approval only and can neither propose nor enter an entry.
